Recognition in another European country is entirely at the discretion of the receiving institution or employer; there is no automatic academic recognition and no procedure that confers it. ⚠ TWO MARKETING CLAIMS ON THE ESBS SIDE THAT MUST NOT BE MISREAD AS EUROPEAN RECOGNITION: (1) ESBS states the title carries 'certificación CUALIFICAM de la Fundación para el Conocimiento Madrimasd para la certificación de la Calidad de los Programas de Máster Profesional' — CUALIFICAM is a voluntary regional QUALITY-certification scheme for NON-official professional masters. It certifies process quality; it does not place a title in MECES, in RUCT, in the EHEA framework, or in any European qualifications register. (2) ESBS then writes 'Su equivalente en el ámbito de los Grados y Másteres universitarios oficiales es el Procedimiento de Acreditación de titulaciones y se realiza bajo los mismos estándares de calidad del Espacio Europeo de Educación Superior.' Read carefully, that sentence claims only that CUALIFICAM is ANALOGOUS to official accreditation and uses similar quality standards — it does NOT claim, and cannot deliver, EHEA qualification status. A reader skimming it would take away 'recognised in the EHEA', which is false. The honest statement is: 60 ECTS of study, a private certificate, and zero automatic portability. The programme DOES carry a full 60 ECTS, which is at least the right volume for a second-cycle qualification (unlike some 25-ECTS 'masters'), so a receiving institution that chose to look at it would find substantive credit — but the choice is theirs and nothing obliges them

notes: DATES: For a FEBRUARY 2028 start the pre-enrolment window falls in AUTUMN 2027. Framework: first week of October 2027 to first week of December 2027 (UPC FAQ). Observed school-level instances of that window: ETSEIB, Feb-2026 entry -- 'Curs 2025-26 Q2 (inici febrer 2026). Preinscripcions obertes: Del 6 d'octubre al 7 de desembre de 2025'; Camins, Feb-2027 entry -- Civil Engineering 30/09/2026-11/11/2026 (results 16/12/2026), Structural & Construction Engineering 07/10/2026-21/10/2026 (results published 22/01/2027). Exact 2027 dates are not yet published by any school; treat 'early October to early December 2027' as the planning window and confirm with the school in mid-2027. | NON-EU: No UPC rule excludes non-EU applicants from the February entry. UPC preinscripcio page: 'Amb el document d'admissio, l'estudiant de fora de la UE pot iniciar els tramits de sol.licitud dels visats que els permetin l'estada al nostre pais per cursar el programa de master universitari.' Programme fitxes state only 'Legalisation of foreign documents: All documents issued in non-EU countries must be legalised and bear the corresponding apostille.' MASTEAM adds: 'You can enrol even if the legalization procedures have not finished, but you should demonstrate that you have at least started the legalization procedures.' THE REAL CONSTRAINT IS THE CLOCK, NOT A RULE. Published February-entry timetables leave 4-8 weeks between the admission decision (which is what unlocks the Spanish student-visa application) and the start of classes: ETSEIB 2026 -- preinscripcio closed 7 Dec 2025, provisional list 16 Jan 2026, definitive early Feb, matricula 11 Feb 2026; Camins Feb-2027 entry -- Civil Engineering applications 30/09/2026-11/11/2026, results 16/12/2026, classes February 2027; ETSETB 2026 -- admitted list published 16 Jan 2026, enrolment 5 Feb, classes 12 Feb. A Tunisian national applying from Tunis needs a Spanish long-stay student visa, routinely 1-3 months from a complete file. MASTEAM's own calendar warns: 'Non-European Union nationals should apply as soon as possible, in order to obtain admission soon enough to proceed with the visa request at the Spanish consulates in their countries.' The February window is therefore legally open but operationally very tight, and is the single most likely point of failure. | FEES: Non-EU non-resident price CONFIRMED at 45,00 EUR/credit for first-time credits (UPC 'Preus i beques', 2026-27: row 'Master universitari habilitant i no habilitant (no residents, no UE)' = 45 EUR, 1a matricula; EU non-qualifying master = 19,37 EUR/credit, matching Decret 96/2026). Cross-checked arithmetically against each programme fitxa: 120 ECTS -> 5.400 EUR (=120x45); 90 ECTS -> 4.050 EUR (=90x45); 60 ECTS -> 2.700 EUR (=60x45). CONFLICT: UPC's own master's FAQ (both CA and EN) states 'Per-credit fees for non-resident foreign students who are non-European Union students (non-EU residents) are EUR102.52 for the NON-qualifying master's degree' -- this figure is irreconcilable with UPC's own fee table and per-programme totals and is treated as stale. Nothing on the fee pages differentiates a February entrant: the price is per credit per matricula, and UPC bills semester-by-semester ('segons el tipus de matricula (anual o quadrimestral)'), so a QP entrant pays the same per-credit rate.
campus: Escola d'Enginyeria de Telecomunicació i Aeroespacial de Castelldefels (EETAC), Campus del Baix Llobregat, Parc Mediterrani de la Tecnologia, Castelldefels — sole teaching centre stated ('Location: Castelldefels School of Telecommunications and Aerospace Engineering'). NOT Barcelona: Castelldefels is a separate coastal town ~20 km south-west of the city
university_awarding: Universitat Politècnica de Catalunya (UPC) — public university, awards the degree in its own name
europe_recognition: EHEA level 7 (Bologna) — academic recognition across the EHEA. Official Spanish máster universitario, MECES 3 = EQF 7, second cycle, Diploma Supplement issued, doctoral access. europe_recognition: EHEA level 7 (Bologna) — academic recognition across the EHEA, on BRIEF case (a). Legal basis, all read off the RUCT detail page for 3500484: official Spanish Máster Universitario, «Nivel MECES: 3» = EQF/EHEA level 7, second cycle, constituted under RD 822/2021, Acuerdo del Consejo de Ministros published in the BOE on 01/10/2025, institutional accreditation renewed 21/10/2024. It carries a Diploma Supplement as of right — UPC charges 218,15 € to issue the official degree certificate with the European Diploma Supplement — and grants access to doctoral study. THE TWO LIMITS THAT MATTER HERE, and the first of them bites unusually hard on this particular degree. (i) EHEA academic recognition is NOT professional recognition, and this master is precisely a case where the difference is substantive rather than theoretical: RUCT records «Habilita para profesión regulada: Sí — Ingeniero Industrial», so what the degree confers in Spain is the legal attribution to practise a REGULATED profession. Those attributions are a Spanish national entitlement. Carrying them into another EU/EEA state is not part of EHEA academic recognition at all — it runs through Directive 2005/36/EC and the receiving state's own competent-authority procedure, which may impose an aptitude test or adaptation period. So a graduate may have their qualification academically recognised in, say, France or Germany while still not being authorised to sign off as an engineer there. Anyone valuing this degree for its habilitante status must understand that the habilitación is the part that travels LEAST well. (ii) Academic recognition abroad still requires the receiving country's own procedure — the EHEA and the Lisbon Recognition Convention make that routine, not automatic. NOTE ON THE STALE LINK: the page's «Official degree — Recorded in the Ministry of Science, Innovation and Universities» link resolves to RUCT 4314000, which has been in extinction since 01/08/2025. That does not weaken the recognition analysis — 4314000 is itself MECES 3 and EQF 7, and anyone who already holds it holds a fully recognised degree — but a 2027 entrant must be enrolled on 3500484, and the recognition evidence to quote is 3500484's, not the link the page gives you.

tuition_non_eu_eur: EUR 5,400 (2026-27 rates) — tuition alone, printed on the page itself. Observed school-level instances of that window: ETSEIB, Feb-2026 entry -- 'Curs 2025-26 Q2 (inici febrer 2026). Preinscripcions obertes: Del 6 d'octubre al 7 de desembre de 2025'; Camins, Feb-2027 entry -- Civil Engineering 30/09/2026-11/11/2026 (results 16/12/2026), Structural & Construction Engineering 07/10/2026-21/10/2026 (results published 22/01/2027). Exact 2027 dates are not yet published by any school; treat 'early October to early December 2027' as the planning window and confirm with the school in mid-2027. | NON-EU: No UPC rule excludes non-EU applicants from the February entry. UPC preinscripcio page: 'Amb el document d'admissio, l'estudiant de fora de la UE pot iniciar els tramits de sol.licitud dels visats que els permetin l'estada al nostre pais per cursar el programa de master universitari.' Programme fitxes state only 'Legalisation of foreign documents: All documents issued in non-EU countries must be legalised and bear the corresponding apostille.' MASTEAM adds: 'You can enrol even if the legalization procedures have not finished, but you should demonstrate that you have at least started the legalization procedures.' THE REAL CONSTRAINT IS THE CLOCK, NOT A RULE. Published February-entry timetables leave 4-8 weeks between the admission decision (which is what unlocks the Spanish student-visa application) and the start of classes: ETSEIB 2026 -- preinscripcio closed 7 Dec 2025, provisional list 16 Jan 2026, definitive early Feb, matricula 11 Feb 2026; Camins Feb-2027 entry -- Civil Engineering applications 30/09/2026-11/11/2026, results 16/12/2026, classes February 2027; ETSETB 2026 -- admitted list published 16 Jan 2026, enrolment 5 Feb, classes 12 Feb. A Tunisian national applying from Tunis needs a Spanish long-stay student visa, routinely 1-3 months from a complete file. MASTEAM's own calendar warns: 'Non-European Union nationals should apply as soon as possible, in order to obtain admission soon enough to proceed with the visa request at the Spanish consulates in their countries.' The February window is therefore legally open but operationally very tight, and is the single most likely point of failure. | FEES: Non-EU non-resident price CONFIRMED at 45,00 EUR/credit for first-time credits (UPC 'Preus i beques', 2026-27: row 'Master universitari habilitant i no habilitant (no residents, no UE)' = 45 EUR, 1a matricula; EU non-qualifying master = 19,37 EUR/credit, matching Decret 96/2026). Cross-checked arithmetically against each programme fitxa: 120 ECTS -> 5.400 EUR (=120x45); 90 ECTS -> 4.050 EUR (=90x45); 60 ECTS -> 2.700 EUR (=60x45). CONFLICT: UPC's own master's FAQ (both CA and EN) states 'Per-credit fees for non-resident foreign students who are non-European Union students (non-EU residents) are EUR102.52 for the NON-qualifying master's degree' -- this figure is irreconcilable with UPC's own fee table and per-programme totals and is treated as stale. Nothing on the fee pages differentiates a February entrant: the price is per credit per matricula, and UPC bills semester-by-semester ('segons el tipus de matricula (anual o quadrimestral)'), so a QP entrant pays the same per-credit rate.
